title: The three rate-limit legs are gated independently, so a venue can be closed to deployment while still open for swaps
content:
The Curve pyUSD/USDC instance publishes inflow "`maxAmount`: 0" and outflow "`maxAmount`: 0" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.7.3.2.4.1/.2) alongside swap limits of "`maxAmount`: 5,000,000, `slope`: 100,000,000 per day, Max slippage: 0.1%" (.7.3.2.4.3).

This is a different configuration from the swap-only instances. Those write "N/A - swap only" — the LP legs are inapplicable. Here they are applicable and explicitly set to zero: liquidity provision to this pool is a defined capability that has been sized to nothing, while trading through it remains fully live.

Read together with the whitelist-by-rate-limit design, the granularity is the point. Permission is not held at the level of the venue but at the level of the (action, venue) pair, so 'Spark may trade against this pool but may not become an LP in it' is expressible as configuration rather than as code or prose. The distinction is real: providing liquidity means holding an LP position exposed to the pool's composition and to pyUSD's peg, whereas swapping through it is momentary.

The practical caution is the same one the zero-limit instances raise throughout: nothing labels this state. An `Active` Curve instance with a populated swap leg and zeroed LP legs looks, in the status hierarchy, exactly like one where all three legs are live. Only reading all three sets of numbers reveals which capabilities are actually granted.
description: Curve pyUSD/USDC sets both inflow and outflow maxAmount to 0 yet keeps swap limits at 5,000,000 with a 100,000,000 per day slope — one venue, two different approval states at once.
